summary: The written past, and the spoken past of sein, haben and the modals.
rule: Two jobs. In writing — narration, reports, anything told rather than said — the Präteritum is the ordinary past tense. In speech it survives for a short list: sein, haben and the modal verbs, where «ich war» and «ich musste» are what people actually say and the Perfekt sounds heavy.
why: One paradigm, twice, with 156 exercises each. The A2 rule is the more complete of the two — it names the mixed verbs and the modal forms — while the B1 copy adds the register point, that the Präteritum is for written narration and for sein/haben/modals in speech. The keeper now carries both, so nothing is lost by retiring the B1 restatement.
